display_name: Fritz Haag Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr Riesling Auslese, Mosel
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr's iron-rich red slate (Braunfelschiefer) and 70-degree south-facing slopes concentrate Riesling flavors into smoky peach and wet stone in this Auslese. Fritz Haag hand-harvests these ultra-ripe clusters from vines averaging 60 years old. Low alcohol around 7-8% keeps the electric acidity front and center.",
  "wine_summary": "Fritz Haag ranks among Mosel's elite estates with 30 hectares mostly in Brauneberg, bottling single-vineyard sites that highlight slate variations. This Auslese from Juffer Sonnenuhr stands out for its balance of ripeness and Mosel transparency, where red slate adds a rare smoky density to the peach and citrus core. The estate's focus on dry and off-dry styles across Prädikats (ripeness levels like Kabinett to Auslese) delivers consistent quality, with silver medals from TEXSOM for 2018 and 2020 vintages underscoring its appeal.",
  "terroir_expression": "Red slate soils in Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr release iron minerals during rain, translating to flinty smoke and blood orange zest in the glass, while the steep exposition and cool Mosel climate (long autumns, 800mm rainfall) build piercing acidity and concentrated white peach. Unlike gray slate's pure graphite edge in neighboring sites, this Braunfelschiefer adds a ferrous, almost bloody depth that lingers through the finish.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-picked in multiple late passes for riper berries, the grapes undergo gentle whole-cluster pressing to extract pure juice without skin bitterness. Slow fermentation in stainless steel at cool temperatures (around 14-16°C) preserves volatile aromas and allows residual sugar to balance the slate-driven acidity— a hallmark of Mosel Prädikat wines where ripeness tiers dictate potential alcohol and sweetness.",
  "food_pairing": "Spicy Sichuan dan dan noodles: the wine's peach sweetness and acidity cut through numbing heat and sesame oil. Foie gras torchon with Sauternes gelée: slate minerality and low alcohol refresh the fatty liver without clashing. Nashville hot chicken sandwich: citrus zip and smoke match the fiery crust while sweetness tempers vinegar brine. Blue cheese soufflé: piercing acidity slices rich dairy, with wet stone echoing the moldy tang. Grilled sardines with lemon and herbs: bracing structure stands up to oily fish, slate grounding the seaside char.",
  "comparable_wines": "Egon Müller Scharzhofberger Riesling Auslese — similar Mosel ripeness and slate focus but with more yellow fruit from gray soils. Joh. Jos. Prüm Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Auslese — matching south-facing site and smoky peach, though Prüm's style leans drier.",
  "style_profile": "Light-bodied off-dry white with laser acidity and red slate smoke",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink from 2025-2040 for vintages like 2020; store cool (10-12°C) on side in 80% humidity to let honeyed notes integrate with minerals. Younger examples like 2020 need 3-5 years to open.",
  "value_assessment": "$70-100 retail. Beats Selbach-Oster's similar Mosel Auslese at $80 by offering denser red slate character from steeper rows. Worth seeking for the site specificity—cheaper Kabinett versions lack this ripeness depth.",
  "market_position": "Riesling collectors and somms chase these on niche lists at upscale German spots or natural wine bars. Retail appears in specialty shops like Astor Wines for enthusiasts tired of basic trocken. Casual off-dry fans discover it via sommelier recs at farm-to-table spots.",
  "insider_take": "Skip this if you demand bone-dry Riesling—the Auslese ripeness trades purity for seductive peach that ages into kerosene magic. Most miss how the low ABV (7%) amplifies food pairing power over higher-octane neighbors. Buy multiples of 2018 or 2020; they outperform medals suggest.",
